name: Portugal
summary_text: Portugal remains one of the world's safest destinations for transgender visitors. The 2018 self-determination law allows legal gender and name change without medical requirements (minors 16-17 with parental consent), bathroom access matching one's gender is legally protected, conversion therapy is banned (2024), intersex infant surgery is banned, and hate-crime law covers gender identity — within an EU rule-of-law environment with very low violent crime. Same-sex marriage since 2010. Two caveats pull it just below its Iberian neighbour Spain. First, in March 2026 the Portuguese parliament approved in first reading three bills (backed by the governing PSD/CDS and the far-right Chega) that would repeal the 2018 self-ID law, reintroduce a mandatory medical opinion, and ban hormones for minors. As of the most recent reporting this is not yet final law — it is in committee, and a government technical opinion warned it may be unconstitutional — so the self-ID framework is still in force. Second, hate-crime reports rose about 38% in both 2023 and 2024, with acknowledged under-reporting. For a visitor these translate to a real political-hostility signal and elevated but still low-level harassment risk, not criminal exposure. The practical day-to-day environment is calm and welcoming, particularly in Lisbon and Porto.

sources.title: Rainbow Map 2026 | ILGA-Europe
sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Rainbow Map 2026 (May 2026): Spain tops the ranking of 49 countries; the map and index document LGBTI human-rights laws and policies across Europe, with commentary on the gap between legal progress and daily experience.
Público (March 2026, in Portuguese): the Portuguese Parliament (AR) approved PSD, Chega and CDS bills reversing the gender-identity law - first vote to roll back self-ID legal gender recognition.

sources.title: Regime da identidade de género revogado? O que pode mudar – Observador
sources.claim_summary: Observador (March 2026, in Portuguese): the right revokes the gender-identity regime - what may change and what each bill provides; PSD, CDS and Chega voted to reverse the regime allowing gender change without medical validation; hormones for minors would be banned.

sources.title: Joint Statement: European LGBTI Organisations call on the Portuguese Parliament to reject bills attacking trans and intersex rights | ILGA-Europe
sources.claim_summary: Joint statement (March 2026) by IGLYO, ILGA-Europe, OII Europe, TGEU, EL*C and Bi+ Equal calling on the Portuguese Parliament to reject three bills attacking trans and intersex rights - a serious attack on rights, dignity, safety and bodily autonomy that would drop Portugal at least 4 places on the Rainbow Map.

sources.title: Portugal Moves Toward Anti-LGBTIQ+ Legislation | Forbidden Colours
sources.claim_summary: Forbidden Colours (March 2026): condemns the approval in general terms of three anti-trans bills (151-79), backed by Chega and governing PSD/CDS-PP; the bills target the self-identification law (Law 38/2018), would reintroduce medical gatekeeping, and one Chega bill bans discussing LGBTIQ+ topics in schools (mirroring Hungary/Russia 'anti-propaganda' laws).

sources.title: Portugal set to roll back trans self-determination law: what’s at stake? -
sources.claim_summary: KET Magazine (March 2026): Portugal set to roll back its trans self-determination law - the first-reading vote would reintroduce a mandatory medical opinion for legal gender/name change, undoing the 2018 reform (self-declaration from 16); human-rights groups warn of medicalised gatekeeping, delays, costs and arbitrary refusals.

sources.title: Comissão confirma que a lei atual de identidade de género está alinhada com padrões internacionais - TVI Notícias
sources.claim_summary: TVI/Lusa (April 2026, in Portuguese): the Commission for Citizenship and Gender Equality (CIG) confirms in a technical analysis that the current gender-identity law is aligned with international standards and that self-determination is protected by the Portuguese Constitution; the Chega bill 'rests on discontinued terminology' and non-consensual definitions.

sources.title: Legal Gender Changes Edge Back Toward Their 2024 Record a...
sources.claim_summary: The Portugal Brief (Aug 2026): legal gender changes edge back toward their 2024 record (606 in 2024, 541 in 2025; ~3,300 total since 2018), concentrated in Lisbon, as Parliament moves to reimpose the medical test the 2018 self-determination law scrapped.

European Parliament written question E-001183/2026 (2026), 'Health and safety of transgender people in Portugal' — an MEP questions the Commission on the repeal process for the 2018 gender self-determination law and its health-and-safety impact on trans people.
OSCE/ODIHR page on Portugal's hate-crime legislation (Decree Law 48/95, amended by Law 15/2024): excerpts including Article 132 aggravated murder with SOGI-related aggravating circumstances.

Equaldex data for Portugal: homosexuality legal, marriage legal, gender change with no restrictions, gender-affirming care legal, full ban on intersex infant surgery, hate-crime protections cover SOGI, discrimination illegal, conversion therapy banned, bathroom access protected. High public support for same-sex parenting (ranked #1 of 30 EU regions).

sources.title: Ombudsman requests a review of the constitutionality of article 176-C of the Penal Code, which establishes the crime of acts contrary to sexual orientation, gender identity or gend
sources.claim_summary: Portuguese Ombudsman: requests a review of the constitutionality of Article 176-C of the Penal Code, which establishes the crime of acts contrary to sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression - an unusual challenge to a protective provision.
